extracted.intended_audience: vision-language and video-understanding researchers, ML practitioners building/evaluating VLMs on video QA, dataset creators
extracted.subtask_description: A benchmark for video question answering on surprising videos (humor, creative, magic) with tasks for counter-intuitive timestamp localization, detailed free-text description, reasoning about counter-intuitiveness, title attribution, and creativity scoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counter-intuitive timestamp localization (H1/C1/M1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Localize the time span (start/end frames) of the counter-intuitive / surprising moment in the video (tasks H1, C1, M1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Localization is evaluated using IOU (Intersection over Union) between predicted span and ground truth. The dataset highlights high-frequency answer time spans and uses IOU as the metric for these tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed video description (H2/C2/M2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Produce a detailed free-text description of what happened during the relevant video segment (tasks H2, C2, M2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responses are free-text and evaluated with text-generation metrics (BLEU-4, ROUGE-L, CIDEr, BLEURT, GPT-4). The benchmark emphasizes in-depth description and notes common model shortcomings such as adding incorrect details (e.g., inventing 'wearing sunglasses').

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasoning around counter-intuitiveness (H3/C3/M3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain why the segment is surprising/funny/creative/magical — reasoning about commonsense violations and the source of surprise (tasks H3, C3, M3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a free-text explanation task requiring interpretation of counter-intuitiveness; evaluated with the same text metrics (BLEU-4/ROUGE-L/CIDEr/BLEURT/GPT-4). Models show significant gaps on visual-centered and counter-intuitive reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attributing a fitting and vivid title (H4/C4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Generate a concise, vivid title that captures the video's 'shine point' or most salient amusing/creative aspect (tasks H4, C4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Title generation is a higher-level free-text task (responses compared via text metrics). Example prompts on the page: 'Please give this humorous short video a vivid and appropriate title.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring the video creativity (C5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assign a creativity score to the video (e.g., on a 0–20 scale for CreativeQA subset).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation metric for this task is Accuracy between the predicted score and the official (annotator) score. The page gives an example: 'Also, score the creativity of the video on a scale of 0 to 20.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Responses in free-text format
rubrics_metrics.description: All tasks' outputs are free-text answers rather than constrained labels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because answers are open-ended, evaluation uses standard text-generation metrics (BLEU-4 / ROUGE-L / CIDEr and semantic metrics BLEURT / GPT-4). The benchmark stresses difficulties in free-text generation for describing and reasoning about surprising content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spatial-temporal reasoning capability
rubrics_metrics.description: Models must demonstrate strong spatial-temporal reasoning to locate events, describe dynamics, and interpret causality in the video.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FunQA specifically targets spatial-temporal reasoning as a core competency (localization, description, reasoning). The paper reports significant performance gaps for existing VLMs on spatial-temporal tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual-centered reasoning (understanding visual evidence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Accurately interpret and ground explanations and descriptions in the visual content (visual-centric reasoning).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The dataset emphasizes visual-centered reasoning as distinct from purely language-based QA; failures include hallucinating visual details or misattributing causes (e.g., wrong explanation for 'throwing ketchup').

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation metrics for free-text responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of multiple automatic metrics to evaluate textual outputs: BLEU-4, ROUGE-L, CIDEr, BLEURT, and GPT-4 (and BLEURT / GPT-4 shown for semantic evaluation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page specifies BLEU-4/ROUGE-L/CIDEr in one row and BLEURT/GPT-4 in another, indicating both n-gram and learned/LM-based evaluators are used to assess quality of descriptions, explanations, and titles.

rubrics_metrics.name: IOU as the localization metric
rubrics_metrics.description: Intersection-over-Union (IOU) is the metric used to evaluate predicted timestamp spans for localization tasks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IOU compares predicted start/end frames to ground-truth spans; used for H1, C1, M1 localization evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annotator consensus / answer reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Dataset includes annotator agreement statistics (percentage of consensus between annotators for the same answer) as a measure of answer reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page reports percentage consensus on sampled sets and shows average answer lengths; these statistics inform expected variability and reliability of free-text ground truth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Known failure modes and anti-patterns
rubrics_metrics.description: Common model errors include hallucinating wrong visual details and misinterpreting the cause of humorous or surprising events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples noted: Video-ChatGPT added incorrect details ('wearing sunglasses'); VideoChat misinterpreted the humorous reason for 'throwing ketchup' as 'knocking over the ketchup bottle'. These are cited as pitfalls to avoid when producing descriptions/explanations.
